description: RiverREM is OpenTopography's maintained Python package for generating river-relative elevation models from digital terrain data. It obtains river centrelines from OpenStreetMap and interpolates river elevations using sampling choices based on terrain resolution and river sinuosity. Inputs are a digital elevation model and optional user-supplied centreline; outputs are relative-elevation rasters and visualisations. Coverage and spatial resolution follow the terrain extent and grid. Source is free under GPL-3.0, with installation examples and parameter documentation. A limitation is that missing or inaccurate river centrelines affect the result; users may need to supply their own geometry. Relative elevation describes floodplain terrain but does not itself calculate inundation probability or hydraulic water levels. RiverREM can prepare terrain context for flood-infrastructure simulations. OpenStreetMap (data-openstreetmap) is its default centreline source. No elevation raster or river geometry was downloaded.
